question.text: Conquistadors from this European nation conquered the Incas. This empire established colonies in all of Central America and most of South America.
question.clue: This country was blamed for a shipwreck near Havana Harbor that destroyed the USS Maine.

swap.leadin: This person names an "exchange" that transferred plants, animals, and diseases between Europe and the Americas.
swap.text: Name this Genoese explorer, who "discovered" the New World in 1492 with the ships Nina [NEEN-yah], Pinta, and Santa Maria.
swap.clue: After becoming dissatisfied with the vast numbers of slaves he sent to Europe, this man's patrons ordered Francisco de Bobadilla to replace him in one administrative post, though he retained the title almirantazgo.

question.leadin: This fleet attempted to meet with the troops of the Duke of Parma but, while waiting at Gravelines, was attacked by the British navy and was forced to go north.
question.text: Identify this fleet that King Philip II of Spain sent to conquer England in 1588.
question.answerHtml: the Spanish Armada [accept Grande y Felicisima Armada or Armada Invencible]
question.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Portuguese colonial history.
swap.text: Later modified by the Treaty of Zaragoza to include the Moluccas, this treaty set up a line of demarcation dividing the world between Spain and Portugal.
swap.clue: This treaty established a line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, which was later extended through both poles by the Treaty of Zaragoza.

question.leadin: This conflict began after the death of the sickly king Charles II.
question.text: Name this conflict in which the Habsburg and Bourbon dynasties fought for the throne of a namesake country.
question.answerHtml: War of the Spanish Succession [do NOT accept or prompt on “Queen Anne’s War”]
question.clue: The collapse of the Grand Alliance was prevented after the Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy won this war's Battle of Blenheim, and the North American theater of this war was Queen Anne's War.

swap.leadin: The Iberian Peninsula was subject to this war movement in resistance to Muslim rule.
swap.text: This period of Iberian history consists of Christians retaking Spain from the Moors.
swap.clue: At the Battle of Covadonga, which sparked this conflict, one empire failed to conquer Asturias.

question.text: Franco was a member of this fascist political movement in Spain that was founded by Primo de Rivera.
question.answerHtml: Falange (or Spanish Phalanx of the Assemblies of the National Syndicalist Offensive)
question.clue: Two leaders of this party were buried within the Santa Cruz Basilica at the Valley of the Fallen.

swap.leadin: The Condor Legion provided bombing support for one side during this war, including during its Battle of the Ebro.
swap.text: Name this war in which the Nationalist forces of Francisco Franco defeated the Republicans.
swap.clue: In this war, the Luftwaffe's Condor Legion bombarded the town of Guernica.

question.leadin: This rival of Emilio Mola originally led the Army of Africa in revolt.
question.text: Name this leader who maintained the Plazas de soberania and signed a Pact with Eisenhower that helped start his country's economic miracle from 1959 to 1973. He was succeeded by Juan Carlos.
question.clue: A confidant of this leader was assassinated by a nationalist organization using the pseudonym of Txikia who dug a tunnel and lined it with bombs in Operation Ogre.

swap.text: The physician Abu al-Qasim did pioneering work on dissections and removing bladder stones in this city. Abd ar-Rahman III ruled from this city, whose massive Great Mosque contained a Court of the Oranges and was converted to a Catholic cathedral in 1236.
swap.clue: Mozarabs like Paul Alvar and Eulogius were hanged in this city during its namesake "Martyrs Movement."

question.text: The transfer of the Portuguese court to Brazil occurred during this regional conflict of the Napoleonic Wars, during which Joseph Bonaparte ascended to the Spanish throne.
question.answerHtml: Peninsular War [or Guerra Peninsular; or Guerra de la Independencia española; prompt on Spanish War of Independence; prompt on French invasion of the Iberian Peninsula; prompt on War of the Sixth Coalition]
question.clue: During this war, defeats at Vitoria and Salamanca undermined the rule of Joseph Bonaparte, who fought against an allied force led by the Duke of Wellington.

swap.leadin: This man's most important work centers on the examination of conscience.
swap.text: Name this man who wrote a work that details an ideal retreat, which is laid out in four weeks, each of which details a segment of the life of Christ, The Spiritual Exercises.
swap.answerHtml: Saint Ignatius of Loyola [prompt on Saint Ignatius; or Ignacio de Loyola]
swap.clue: This theologian was canonized by Gregory XV and spent a year praying in a cave near Manresa.

question.leadin: This autonomous community contains the provinces of Malaga and Cadiz.
question.text: Name this southernmost autonomous community of Spain that contains the city of Granada.
question.clue: This region is also home to the city of Cadiz, which, owing to its strategic position, was raided by Sir Francis Drake seeking to impede the Spanish Armada and blockaded by Lord Nelson before the Battle of Trafalgar.

swap.leadin: A descendant of the Duchy of Vascony, its southern part was eventually absorbed by Castille.
swap.text: Identify this kingdom spanning the Pyrenees ruled by kings like Sancho the Great, which had its capital at Pamplona and once shared its name with that city.
swap.clue: Another ruler of this kingdom was offered the French crown by Etienne Marcel during the Jacquerie.

question.leadin: The evolution of the queen from one of the weakest chess pieces to the strongest began in Spain under this ruler.
question.text: Name this "Catholic monarch" who completed the Reconquista and began the Spanish Inquisition with her husband Ferdinand II.
question.clue: This mother of Juana the Mad conquered the kingdom of Granada and, along with her husband, expelled all Jews from their lands through the Alhambra Decree.

swap.leadin: This man was exiled after the unauthorized Battle of Cabra, which angered Alfonso VI.
swap.text: Name this man who spent around six years serving the Moorish leader of Zaragoza, during which he frequently fought such Christian kingdoms as Aragon and also earned a nickname that probably means "The Lord."
swap.answerHtml: El Cid (el seed or el theeth) [or Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar; accept El Campeador]
swap.clue: This ruler of Valencia who fought both for and against the Taifa of Zargoza.

question.text: This conservative Spanish prime minister switched places with Liberal Praxedes Mateo Sagasta during the turno pacifico. His support of the Carlists led to his 1897 assassination by Italian anarchist Michel Angiolillo.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about early modern European cartography.
swap.text: In 1767, ambassador Ferdinando Galiani found a "treasure trove" of parchment maps produced earlier under the rule of this kingdom. Centuries earlier, mercenaries from this kingdom were led by Roger de Flor ("roo-ZHAY duh FLO").
swap.answerHtml: Aragon [or Reino d’Aragón or Regne d’Aragó; prompt on Naples by asking “under the rule of what kingdom?”]
swap.clue: This polity conquered Sicily in the wake of the Sicilian Vespers Uprising in 1282 during the reign of its "Great" king, Peter III.

question.leadin: This polity produced antipope Benedict XIII, who was backed its King Alfonso V the Magnanimous against Pope Martin V and the Sforzas. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this kingdom which under Alfonso incorporated Naples and Valencia, whose most revered King may have been John the Great, who faced a civil war following the birth of his son Charles of Viana that eventually forced him to relinquish Rousillon to Louis XI, and who would later become the grandfather of Joana the Mad.
question.clue: A princess of this kingdom was the first woman named as an ambassador to another European nation, in this case England.

swap.leadin: This man's prime minister was Antonio Canovas del Castillo, and he took power following Arsenio Martinez-Campos proclaimed him king at Sagunto.
swap.text: Name this Spanish king, who took power after the fall of the first Spanish republic.
swap.clue: This man, who spent part of his time in exile attending Sandhurst College, returned to Spain and was proclaimed king following the overthrow of the First Spanish Republic. Antonio Canovas de Castillo promulgated the royalist constitution during this monarch's reign in 1876.
